heroHeadline: Ukraine Destroys Russian Drone Pilot Training Camp — 65 Cadets Killed in Snizhne Strike; Russia Net Loses 69 Sq Miles Over 4 Weeks as Drone Attrition Sets Records
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,547 of Russia's full-scale invasion, Ukraine executed a precision drone strike on a Russian military drone pilot training camp in Snizhne, Russian-occupied Donetsk Oblast, killing 65 cadets and 1 instructor — one of the most significant single strikes against Russian drone training infrastructure in the war. The attack is part of Ukraine's broader 2026 mid-range strike campaign, which has doubled in tempo since March. Overnight into May 20 (Day 1,546), Russia launched 116 drones at Ukraine; 109 were intercepted but strikes hit Kharkiv's Chuhuiv community and an industrial facility in Kryvyi Rih. Ukrainian drone units set a record pace, striking 19,203 Russian military personnel in the first 19 days of May alone, per the commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces. The Russia Matters War Report Card (released May 20) documented Russia's net loss of 69 square miles of Ukrainian territory over four weeks (April 21–May 19), with Russia's daily advance rate falling from 9.76 sq km/day in early 2025 to just 2.9 sq km/day in May 2026. NATO allies convened in Brussels on May 20 after inconclusive peace talks in Moscow; Ukraine and Hungary simultaneously launched expert-level bilateral consultations — the first substantive talks since Péter Magyar's government replaced Orbán in April. Russian cumulative military losses reached 1,352,980 personnel as of May 21 (+910 in the last 24 hours).
